narrative.summary: On 2014-12-02 between 04:14 and 04:17 UTC, the SW-AUTH-001 detector (rules-v1) recorded four bursts of failed SSH logins on asset GOV-VPN-01. The bursts were: 74 failures in 60 s (all for non-existent users) from one source targeting 13 usernames (markus, mira, oi-dev, ondra, plugins); 71 failures in 60 s from one source targeting 13 usernames (compras, deisimar, desliga, esau, gerencia); 65 failures in 60 s from one source targeting 15 usernames (tiago, vendas, samba, apache, exclusive_table); and 24 failures in 60 s from one source targeting 4 usernames (kushal, rashiya, root2, santosh). The events are identified by evidence IDs 55b2d9fb92cbe3b3c81b6639:SR-SSH-20141202T0414, 55b2d9fb92cbe3b3c81b6639:SR-SSH-20141202T0415, 55b2d9fb92cbe3b3c81b6639:SR-SSH-20141202T0416, 55b2d9fb92cbe3b3c81b6639:SR-SSH-20141202T0417.
narrative.why_relevant: These stored observations merit analyst review because they show repeated authentication attempts against non-existent accounts from a single source within short windows. The heuristic suggests possible brute-force activity, but the data do not confirm a successful compromise; the sensor records only failures and does not capture any later successful logins or related process telemetry. No known CVE linkage or vendor patch is associated with these events.
recommended_actions: Review the stored source evidence and validate sensor coverage
Check the login service's success log for the same window: failures alone do not show whether a guess worked
Rate-limit or block the failing sources at the edge and confirm no listed username exists with a weak password
